name: airapvideo
tagline: Upload a photo, get a vertical lip-synced rap video with a beat and a stage behind it.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a pipeline, not an invention: face detect, lip-sync a face to an audio track, mix the vocal over a beat, composite to 1080x1920, burn captions, export. Every stage has an off-the-shelf model or an ffmpeg flag behind it, so an agent can wire the whole chain in a weekend. The catch is that none of those models will run on a laptop pleasantly, so you are either buying a GPU hour or renting inference, and the rap vocal itself is the part you cannot fake with ffmpeg. Quality is also where the gap shows: their output is tuned, yours will have mushy mouths on profile shots and a vocal that sits badly on the beat until you fight the mix. Fine for making your friends laugh, worse than the paid version for anything you would post.
coreLoopDIY: A local web page where you upload a portrait, paste lyrics, pick a beat, and get back a downloadable 1080x1920 lip-synced rap clip with burned-in captions.
requirements: An inference API token (Replicate or similar) or a local GPU with 12GB+ VRAM
A vocal source: a music/voice generation API, or your own recorded rap
ffmpeg with libx264 and the drawtext or subtitles filter
A folder of beats you actually have the rights to use
Python 3.11 and the patience to re-render a job four times
whatYouLose: Tuned defaults: their mouth tracking and vocal timing are already fought with, yours is not
Someone else's GPU queue, so your render is as fast as whatever card you are paying for
A phone-shaped flow, upload and share in thirty seconds without touching a terminal
Beat library and any pretense of licensing clarity on what you generated
Graceful failure on bad inputs: sunglasses, side profiles, group photos, low light
moatNotes: The models are rented, not owned. What they actually sell is the parameter sweep nobody wants to redo and a GPU bill that is already paid.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the output is the product and the output is fiddly. Anyone can chain a lip-sync model to ffmpeg, but the difference between a clip that looks like a meme and a clip that looks like a mistake lives in a hundred small defaults: crop ratio, mouth region padding, vocal compression, how captions land on the beat. People paying for this want a video in the next three minutes, not a weekend spent discovering that face alignment hates hats. Add the fact that running the models yourself means either a GPU or an inference bill anyway, and the per-video price stops looking unreasonable.
notes: The novelty wears off around clip four, which is a decent argument for renting it rather than building it.
prompt:
Build a local single-user web app that turns a portrait photo into a vertical lip-synced rap video.

Stack, no substitutions: Python 3.11, FastAPI, one server-rendered HTML page with vanilla JS, SQLite for job state, ffmpeg for all audio and video composition. No React, no user accounts, no cloud deploy, no telemetry, no analytics.

Flow:
1. Page has: a photo upload field, a lyrics textarea, a dropdown of beats read from ./beats/*.mp3, and a Generate button.
2. POST creates a job row in SQLite with status queued and returns a job id. The page polls GET /jobs/{id} every 2 seconds and shows the current stage.
3. Worker runs as a FastAPI BackgroundTask, one job at a time, writing intermediates to ./work/{job_id}/.

Pipeline stages, each a separate function with its own retry and its own log line:
- Validate the photo: detect exactly one frontal face, reject anything else with a clear message. Center-crop to a square around the face.
- Produce the vocal track. Call a hosted model through an HTTP client behind a VocalProvider interface, token from .env. Also support a local-file mode where I drop my own recorded vocal at ./work/{job_id}/vocal.wav and the stage is skipped entirely. Implement the local-file mode first so the pipeline is testable without spending money.
- Mix: ffmpeg amix of vocal over the chosen beat, sidechain-free, vocal 3dB hot, normalize to -14 LUFS.
- Lip-sync: send the cropped photo and the mixed audio to a hosted lip-sync model (wav2lip-class) behind a LipSyncProvider interface, token from .env. Save the returned mp4.
- Compose: ffmpeg scale and pad the talking head onto a 1080x1920 canvas over a still background from ./backgrounds/, burn the lyrics as captions using the subtitles filter from an SRT generated by splitting lyrics evenly across the audio duration. Encode h264, yuv420p, faststart.
4. GET /jobs/{id}/download serves the final mp4.

Also ship: .env.example with the two API tokens and nothing else, a README with ffmpeg install notes and the local-vocal test path, and one end-to-end test that runs the whole pipeline on a bundled sample photo and a 5 second wav with both providers stubbed.

Out of scope, do not build: payments, sharing links, multi-face scenes, animated backgrounds, voice cloning, mobile app, queue scaling.

Be explicit in the README about the fact that beats in ./beats and anything a hosted model returns are my licensing problem, not the app's.
